markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (100%)** · Confident · Read in turn
Single-class conformal set, second-model agreement, typical image. [F1]

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 100%, Normal 0% | Very high |
| Conformal set | {Benign} at 90% | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.99 / 52nd percentile | Typical, reliable input |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Yes | Same top class |
| Similar cases | 4 of 5 Benign | Mostly agree; one Normal |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor-infiltrating stroma** (region 9) · ↓ invasive · Score below typical; no invasion signal · Validated [F2]
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 5, 7, 9) · ↓ invasive · Above typical; linked to lower invasive likelihood · Validated [F3]
- **Tumor cell fraction and density** (regions 0, 9, 10) · context · Both at 97th percentile; high for a Benign suggestion · Measured [F7] [F8]
- **Nuclear size** (regions 0, 9, 10) · context · Lowest mean in reference set · Measured [F9]

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Top-3 deletion drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful.
- **Concepts**: Deletion effect 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007) includes 0: not shown to reflect the classifier. TILs is Unreliable (8/20).

## Could be wrong if
- The 97th-percentile tumor-cell fraction is real, in which case Benign is wrong.
- Conformal coverage is dataset-level; this case can still fall outside the set.

## Check on the slide
1. **0, 9, 10:** Confirm dense small nuclei are benign epithelium, not tumor.
2. **9:** Check for stromal invasion and pleomorphism; the model scored both low.
3. **5, 7, 9:** Verify glandular architecture is benign, not invasive tubules.
